Testimony ofSenator Anne Carney introducing _ 111994;-An Act to Provide Immunity from Civil Liability for Justices of the Peace
before the Joint Standing Committee on Judiciary January 21, 2026
Chair Kuhn and esteemed members of the Joint Standing Committee on the Judiciary, my name is Anne Carney, I represent Senate District 29 and I am honored to introduce LD 1994, "An Act
to Provide Immunity from Civil Liability for Justices of the Peace."
This legislation seeks to modernize the justice of the peace statute to provide justices of the peace the same immunity from civil liability currently granted to all other appointees serving as judicial officers or in quasi-judicial roles. Without statutory protection from liability, highly
qualified prospective and new justices of the peace may be hesitant to pursue the role, potentially
compromising courts' capacity to efficiently review emergency orders including Extreme Risk Protection Orders, Involuntary Commitments, Search Warrants and Arrest Warrants.
I urge you to support LD 1994 as a simple fix to an outdated statute, ensuring all judicial officers
receive the same protections when acting in their official capacity moving forward.

Judicial Branch testimony in favor of I;-;"1994, An Act to Provide Immunity
from Civil Liability for Justices of the Peace:

Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn, members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Judiciary, my name is Julie Finn and I represent the Judicial Branch. I would like to provide some brief testimony in support of Judicial Branch bill, LD 1994.
Justices of the Peace (JPs) assist with non-court hours emergency orders review. This includes Extreme Risk Protection Orders, Involuntary Commitments, Search Warrants, and
Arrest Warrants. We have found that some very qualified potential new JPs do not wish to serve
if there is a question of liability. In addition, some current JPs, after finding out there was no statutory protection, have voiced a concern about continuing in the role. After looking into this
issue, we discovered that all other persons who are appointed to serve as a judicial officer or serve in a quasi-judicial role have statutory immunity (Bail Commissioners, GALs, Mediators,
etc.) The JP statute is quite old, and likely the addition of liability was overlooked at the time of drafting. JPs should have the same protection as other judicial officers when acting in that
capacity.
Thank you for your time.

JAF testimony, 1/21/26
